added_claim_errors: United's travel credits are typically valid for one year, and a one-year ask is reasonable and standard: unverifiable United policy claim, and it contradicts the key's 5-year minimum for a credit in lieu of a refund
Weather affects what the airline owes in compensation and rebooking: vague and misleading, since US law has no cash compensation for a weather cancellation
Draft says the credit is accepted rather than a refund: this has the person give up the cash refund, which is the opposite of what the key advises
A credit is typically good for about a year and 'at least a year' is roughly the standard: contradicts the key's 5-year minimum for a credit in lieu of a refund
A credit is tied to your name and can't be cashed out: generic claim, not verified
A DOT complaint usually unblocks it: unverifiable generalization

The quote 'applies irrespective of the reason for a cancellation' and the claim that airlines must disclose refund rights before offering a credit: both checked and confirmed in the govinfo Federal Register page it links (FR 2024-04-26, 2024-07177), so these are not errors

reasons: B opens by correcting the agent's premise and tells the person not to take the credit. It then drafts a refund request for $412 to the original payment method under DOT's rule, with the 7-business-day deadline for a credit card, and gives a working link to the final rule. I opened that rule on govinfo and confirmed B's quoted sentence and its disclosure claim. A drafts the message the person asked for, which accepts the credit and gives up the cash refund. It mentions the DOT refund right only in a note after the draft, and it calls a one-year credit standard and reasonable. It gives no refund deadline. Both answers miss the 5-year minimum validity, but B's draft protects the $412 and A's does not.
